Then when I rose with the affair, one party broke faith, another went out of it, and others deviated — as though they had not heard the word of God, glory be to Him, where He says: “That is the abode of the hereafter; We appoint it for those who desire neither exaltation in the earth nor corruption; and the outcome is for the God-fearing.” Nay, by God, they had heard it and grasped it; but the world was made sweet in their eyes and its ornament dazzled them.
90:4: But by Him who split the seed and created the soul, were it not for the presence of the one present, and the establishing of the proof by the existence of a helper, and what God has taken upon the scholars — that they should not acquiesce in the gluttony of a wrongdoer nor in the hunger of the wronged — I would have cast its rope upon its own withers, and watered its last with the cup of its first; and you would have found this world of yours of less worth to me than the sneeze of a goat.
90:5: They said: And a man of the people of the Sawad rose to him when he had reached this point in his sermon, and handed him a letter; and he began to look into it. When he had finished reading it, Ibn 'Abbas, may God have mercy on him, said to him: O
91:0: Commander of the Faithful, if only you would carry your words on from where you left off. He said: Far from it, Ibn 'Abbas. That was a froth of the camel's rage: it bubbled up, and then it subsided. Ibn 'Abbas said: By God, I have never grieved over any speech as I grieved over this speech, that the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, did not reach in it the point he intended. [2]
91:1: Ibn Abi al-Hadid said: As for Ibn 'Abbas's words, “I never grieved over any speech” — my shaykh Abu al-Khayr Musaddiq b. Shabib al-Wasiti related to me in the year six hundred and three, saying: I read this sermon to the shaykh Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah b. Ahmad, known as Ibn al-Khashshab; and when I reached this place he said to me: Had I heard Ibn 'Abbas say this, I would have said to him: And did there remain in your cousin's soul any matter he did not reach in this sermon, that you should grieve he did not attain of his speech what he intended? By God, he spared neither the first of them nor the last. [3]
91:2: And in the Bihar, from Kashf al-Yaqin, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: I used to watch for the anger of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, when he mentioned something, or when a report stirred him. Then one day some of his partisans in Syria wrote to him, mentioning in his letter that Mu'awiya, 'Amr b. al-'As, 'Utba b. Abi Sufyan, al-Walid b. 'Uqba and Marwan had gathered before Mu'awiya and had mentioned the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, and reviled him, and had put about among the people that he disparages the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and mentions each one of them with what he deserves.
91:3: And that was when he, peace be upon him, had ordered his companions to wait for him at al-Nukhayla, and they entered Kufa and left him; and that weighed heavily upon him.
91:4: And this report came; so I came to his door by night and said: O Qanbar, what is the news of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him? He said: He is asleep. But he, peace be upon him, heard my words and said: Who is this?
91:5: I said: Ibn 'Abbas, O Commander of the Faithful. He said: Enter. So I entered, and there he was, seated apart from his bed in a single garment, in the posture of one troubled. I said: What ails you this night, Commander of the Faithful? He said: Woe to you, Ibn 'Abbas; and how
91:n2: Nahj al-Balagha, vol. 1, pp. 37-44; Nahj al-Balagha (Subhi), p. 48.
91:n3: The commentary of Ibn Abi al-Hadid, p. 205.
92:0: should the eyes sleep of one whose heart is occupied? O Ibn 'Abbas, your heart is the king of your limbs; and when it is made afraid, sleep flies from it. Here I am, as you see, since the beginning of the night: thought and sleeplessness have seized me, for what has gone before of the breaking of the covenant of the first of this community, for whom the breaking of her covenant was decreed.
92:1: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, commanded those whom he commanded of his companions to greet me in his lifetime as Commander of the Faithful; and I was made certain that I should be so after his death. O Ibn 'Abbas, I am the most entitled of people to the people after him; but matters combined upon the people's desire for this world, and its commanding and its forbidding, and the turning of the hearts of its people away from me.
92:2: I say: and he carried his words on, peace be upon him, in complaint of those who went before him, until he said, peace be upon him: And now, Ibn 'Abbas, I am coupled with the son of the eater of livers, and with 'Amr and 'Utba and al-Walid and Marwan and their followers. When did it ever stir in my breast, or fall into my mind, that the affair would be led away to a world in which these should be chiefs, obeyed? And here they are, at the remembrance of the friends of the Merciful, disparaging them [4] and casting at them enormities, of forged calumny and of rancour long preceding.
92:3: And those entrusted with its keeping, of those who remain of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, know well that the generality of my enemies are of those who answered Satan against me, and whom the people made to shine, and who obeyed his own desire in what harms him in his hereafter. And in God, mighty and exalted, is sufficiency; and He is the granter of right guidance and of soundness. O Ibn 'Abbas, woe to him who wronged me and pushed away my right and did away with the greatness of my station. Where were those men,
92:4: while I was praying with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, a small boy upon whom no prayer was yet enjoined — and they were worshippers of idols and rebels against the Merciful, and by them the fires are kindled?
92:5: Then, when the turning aside of cheeks [5] and the wretchedness of fortunes drew near, they submitted unwillingly and concealed other than what they showed, coveting to put out the light of God; and they waited for the ending of the Messenger's affair and the passing of his term, when
92:n5: Sa'ara khaddahu tas'iran, and sa'arahu, and as'arahu: he turned it away from looking at people out of disdain. Al-ta's: perdition. And al-judud is the plural of al-jadd, with fatha, meaning fortune.
93:0: they had made their souls covet his killing, and their counsel in their house of assembly. God, mighty and exalted, said: “And they schemed, and God schemed; and God is the best of schemers.” [6] And He said: “They wish to put out the light of God with their mouths, and God refuses aught but to complete His light, though the polytheists be averse.” [7]
93:1: O Ibn 'Abbas, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, called them in his lifetime, by a revelation from God, commanding them to take me as their friend; and the people bore what they bore of what the accursed one bore of envy towards our father Adam — so that he went out from the spirit of God and His good pleasure, and the curse was fastened upon him, for his envy of the friend of God. And that will not harm me in anything, God willing. O Ibn 'Abbas, every man wished to be a head, obeyed, to whom the world and his kinsmen should incline; so his desire carried him, and the sweetness of his world, and the people's following after him, to be angry at what had been appointed for me. And were it not for my fear for the lesser of the two weighty things — that it should be cast away, and the tree of knowledge be cut off, and the flower of the world, and the firm rope of God, and His trusted stronghold, and the children of the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds — then the seeking of death and the going forth to God, mighty and exalted, would have been dearer to me than a draught to the thirsty and than sleep to the drowsy. But I was patient, and in the breast are troubles and in the soul are whisperings: “so a comely patience; and God is He whose help is sought against what you describe.”
93:2: And of old were the prophets wronged and the friends of God slain — until he said: “And the unbeliever shall know for whom is the final abode.” And the caller gave the call to prayer, and he said: The prayer, Ibn 'Abbas; let it not be missed. I ask God's forgiveness for myself and for you; and God suffices us and is the best trustee; and there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. Ibn 'Abbas said: And the ending of the night grieved me, and I was filled with regret at its going. [8]
93:n8: Bihar al-Anwar, the Book of Trials and Tribulations, old edition, p. 162 (the conversation of Ibn 'Abbas with the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him).
94:0: Section [the objection of twelve men of the Emigrants and the Ansar to Abu Bakr over what took place after him]. A number of our companions related in their compilations that when the affair was complete for Abu Bakr, and he mounted the pulpit and sat in the seat of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, twelve men objected to that against Abu Bakr: six of the Emigrants — and they are Khalid b. Sa'id b. al-'As, who was of the Banu Umayya; Salman the Persian; Abu Dharr al-Ghifari; al-Miqdad b. al-Aswad; 'Ammar b. Yasir; and Burayda al-Aslami — and six of the Ansar — and they are Abu al-Haytham b. al-Tayyihan; Sahl and 'Uthman the sons of Hunayf; Khuzayma b. Thabit, he of the two testimonies; Ubayy b. Ka'b; and Abu Ayyub al-Ansari.
94:1: He said: When Abu Bakr mounted the pulpit they took counsel among themselves, and some of them said to others: By God, we shall go to him and bring him down from the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. And others of them said: By God, if you do that you will have helped against your own selves; and God, mighty and exalted, has said: “And do not cast yourselves by your own hands into destruction.” [1] So come with us to the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, that we may consult him and learn his opinion. So the people went, all together, to the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, and said: O Commander of the Faithful, you have left a right of which you are the more entitled and the more deserving; for we heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, say:
95:0: 'Ali is with the truth and the truth is with 'Ali; he inclines with the truth wherever it inclines. And we had resolved to go to him and bring him down from the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family; so we have come to you to consult you and to learn your opinion as to what you command us. The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: By God, had you done that, you would have been nothing but a war against them; nor would you have been but as the kohl in the eye, or as the salt in the provision. The community has agreed upon him — the community that has abandoned the word of its prophet and lied against its Lord. I consulted my household about that, and they would have nothing but silence, for what they know of the rancour [1] of the people's breasts and their hatred of God, mighty and exalted, and of the people of the house of His prophet; and that they are seeking the blood-vengeances of the age of ignorance. — until he said, peace be upon him: But go to the man and tell him what you heard from your prophet, and do not leave him in doubt concerning his affair, that it may be the greater proof against him and the more effective in his punishment when he comes to his Lord, having disobeyed his prophet and opposed his command. So they went, until they stood about the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family — and it was a Friday.
95:1: When Abu Bakr mounted the pulpit, each one of them spoke words concerning the right of 'Ali, peace be upon him, and his merit, and what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, had said concerning him — which we have passed over, seeking brevity. The first of them to begin the speaking was Khalid b. Sa'id b. al-'As, then the rest of the Emigrants, then after them the Ansar. And it is related that when they had finished their speech, Abu Bakr was struck dumb upon the pulpit, until he said: I have been given charge of you, and I am not the best of you; release me, release me. 'Umar b. al-Khattab said: Come down from it, you fool! If you cannot stand against the arguments of Quraysh, why did you set yourself in this station? By God, I have a mind to depose you and to set it in Salim the freedman of Abu Hudhayfa. He said: So he came down; then he took his hand and went off to his dwelling. And they remained three days without entering the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family.
95:2: Then on the fourth day Khalid b. al-Walid came to them, and with him a thousand men, and said to them: What is this sitting of yours?
95:3: By God, the Banu Hashim have set their hopes upon it. And Salim the freedman of Abu Hudhayfa came to them, and with him a thousand
96:0: men; and Mu'adh b. Jabal came to them, and with him a thousand men. And man after man kept gathering until four thousand men were gathered. They went out with their swords drawn, 'Umar b. al-Khattab at their head, until they halted in the mosque of the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family. And 'Umar said: By God, O companions of 'Ali, if any man of you goes on to speak as he spoke yesterday, we shall take that in which his two eyes are.
96:1: Khalid b. Sa'id b. al-'As rose to him and said: O son of Suhak the Abyssinian, is it with your swords that you threaten us, or with your numbers that you would frighten us?
96:2: By God, our swords are keener than your swords, and we are the more, though we be few — for the proof of God is among us. By God, did I not know that obedience to my Imam is the more binding upon me, I would have drawn my sword and striven against you in God until I had discharged my excuse. [2] The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said to him: Sit down, Khalid; God has known your station and has thanked you for your striving. So he sat.
96:3: And Salman the Persian, may God be pleased with him, rose to him and said: God is greatest, God is greatest! I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family — and otherwise may I be struck dumb — say: While my brother and the son of my uncle is seated in my mosque with a number of his companions, a company of the dogs of the people of the Fire shall fall upon him, seeking to kill him and to kill those with him. And I do not doubt — indeed, you are they. 'Umar b. al-Khattab made to set upon him, and the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, sprang at him and seized the gathers of his garment and threw him to the ground, and then said: O son of Suhak the Abyssinian, were it not for a writ from God that has preceded and a covenant from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, that has gone before, I would have shown you which of us is the weaker in helpers and the fewer in number. Then he turned to his companions and said: Disperse, may God have mercy on you. By God, I shall not enter the mosque save as my two brothers Musa and Harun entered, when his companions said to him: “Go, you and your Lord, and fight; we are sitting here.” By God, I shall not enter save to visit the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, or for a case that I must judge; for it is not lawful for a proof whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, has established to leave the people in bewilderment. [3]
96:n2: Ablahu 'udhran: that is, he discharged it to him.
96:n3: Al-Ihtijaj, vol. 1, p. 97; Bihar al-Anwar, vol. 28, p. 189.
97:0: Section (on the mention of a sermon he delivered to the people). Al-Shaykh al-Kulayni related in al-Rawda, with his chain, from Abu al-Haytham al-Tayyihan, that the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, addressed the people at Medina and said: Praise belongs to God, beside whom there is no god; He was living without how, and there was no “was” for Him — and he mentioned his words, peace be upon him, in the praise of God and the blessing upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, until he said, addressing the people: By Him who split the seed and created the soul, had you taken knowledge from its mine, and drunk the water in its sweetness, and stored up the good from its place, and taken of the road its clear part, and travelled of the truth its open way, the paths would have been made plain [1] for you, and the signposts would have appeared to you, and Islam would have shone for you; and you would have eaten in plenty, and no poor man among you would have been in want, nor would any Muslim or protected person among you have been wronged. But you travelled the road of darkness, so your world was darkened upon you for all its breadth [2], and the doors of knowledge were shut upon you. So you spoke by your desires and differed in your religion, and gave judgement in the religion of God without knowledge, and followed the misguided and they misguided you, and left the Imams and they left you. So you became such as judge by your desires: when a matter is mentioned you ask the people of the reminder, and when they give you judgement you say: This is knowledge itself. How so — when you have left it and cast it away and opposed it? Gently: in a little while you will reap all that you have sown, and find the evil consequence of what you have committed
97:n1: Nahaja: that is, it became clear.
98:0: and of what you have brought upon yourselves. By Him who split the seed and created the soul, you knew that I am your companion, and he whom you were commanded to obey; and that I am your learned one, by whose knowledge is your deliverance, and the legatee of your prophet, may God bless him and his Family, and the chosen of your Lord, and the tongue of your light, and the one who knows what sets you right. So in a little while, gently, there will come down upon you what you were promised, and what came down upon the nations before you. And God, mighty and exalted, will ask you concerning your Imams: with them you will be gathered, and to God, mighty and exalted, you will come tomorrow.
98:1: By God, had I the number of the companions of Talut, or the number of the people of Badr, and they your equals [a variant: your enemies], I would strike you with the sword until you returned to the truth and turned back to what is true. That would be the better mending of the rent and the surer taking of gentleness. O God, judge between us with the truth; and You are the best of judges.
98:2: He said: Then he went out, peace be upon him, from the mosque and passed by a fold [3] in which were about thirty sheep, and he said: By God, had I men sincere to God, mighty and exalted, and to His Messenger, may God bless him and his Family, to the number of these sheep, I would remove the son of the eater of flies [4] from his rule.
98:3: He said: And when evening came, three hundred and sixty men pledged to him unto death. And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said to them: Come with us in the morning to Ahjar al-Zayt [5], with heads shaven. And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, shaved his head; and none of the people came with head shaven save Abu Dharr, al-Miqdad, Hudhayfa al-Yaman and 'Ammar b. Yasir; and Salman came at the end of the company.
98:4: So he raised his hands, peace be upon him, to the sky and said: O God, the people have held me weak as the Children of Israel held Harun weak. O God, You know what we hide and what we make public, and nothing is hidden from You in the earth or in the sky. Take me as a Muslim, and join me to the righteous. But by the House, and by him who goes
98:n3: Al-sira: an enclosure made of stones and the branches of trees, for sheep and cattle.
98:n4: Al-dhibban, with kasra and doubling: the plural of dhubab, flies. And by “the son of her who ate them” he alluded to the ruler of the time; for in the age of ignorance they used to eat of every foul thing they came by.
98:n5: Ahjar al-Zayt: a place within Medina.
98:n6: “And he who goes to the House”: that is, one who touches it with his hand.
99:0: to the House [6] — and in another copy: and by al-Muzdalifa and those who go lightly to the casting of the pebbles — were it not for a covenant that the unlettered Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, made with me, I would have brought the opponents down to the gulf of death, and sent upon them the downpours of the thunderbolts of death; and in a little while they shall know. [7]
